findings.reason: a node following the constraint literally builds an attempt-keyed reservation that fails on the exact door pairing the Why names, so the node must be told either to key the reservation per run or to make both doors derive the attempt from one source.
findings.text: the "One holder" constraint says reusing `claim_next_attempt` "on the dispatch path means numbering from the attempt being launched", but the two doors derive that number from different sources: `claim_next_attempt` claims `record["attempt"] + 1` from the pointer (reckon/crew/resumption.py:398, called with the pointer record at :1705), while the dispatch door computes the attempt as the last committed attempt plus one (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2735-2745). In the window the Why describes the pointer already carries attempt 2 (written at dispatch.py:3082 after `_create_worktree`) while the last committed attempt is 1, so a resume claims 3 and a dispatch reserves 2 — two keys, two holders, and the dispatch-beside-resume race the section exists to close is admitted

findings.reason: the followup and the section prescribe opposite mechanisms for in-harness launches, so a node reading the followup would build the reservation the section forbids and test for a freeing rule that cannot exist.
findings.text: `f-arolw-013`, the one hand-off a build node reads before the section, says "every relaunch of an existing run id, CLI or in-harness, takes a reservation before the worktree is touched", while §13 now states "An in-harness relaunch therefore takes no reservation" because nothing on disk records a session's end

findings.reason: the release-on-refusal path is what keeps the Deliverable's second clause true ("no launch that has ended, or been killed, leaves the run unlaunchable"), and a case with no control cannot show that guard is present rather than assumed.
findings.text: the Done when asserts "one case per hazard" but the admit-door bullet packs two ("becomes launchable again once its recorded supervisor has exited, and a launch refused before its spawn releases its reservation at once"), and the logged negative controls redden only the first half, so nothing shows the refused-launch release fires

response_events.note: §13's one-holder constraint now requires every door to key the reservation on the same attempt number from one source, the last committed attempt plus one, not the pointer, with a resume-beside-dispatch case.
f-arolw-013 now says CLI relaunches reserve and an in-harness relaunch takes none and is refused while one is held.
§13 splits the admit-door bullet into two cases, each with its own control; the refused-launch release has one.
